title: How to find your results and your profile
summary: Find the competition you shot in and your name in its results table; from there you can open your shooter profile.

body.html: After a Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting competition, its results appear on ClayArena. At some events they are updated while the shooting is still going on. The simplest way is to open that competition and find your name in the results table. You can find the competition in the list of competitions or in the calendar, which shows finished events too.

The table shows your place and how many targets you broke. A round is 25 targets, and your total is the sum of your rounds. An international Sporting™ competition is usually 200 targets, shot in rounds of 25. Club shoots often have fewer targets: the organiser sets the format. How to read the table: How to read a scoreboard and results.

From the results table you can open your shooter profile. It gathers your competitions that are on ClayArena and your key figures. You can also look for yourself in the list of shooters, which can be filtered by country.

Names on the site are written as in the competition documents. International events usually use Latin letters. National events may use the local alphabet, for example Cyrillic letters at Ukrainian events. If you cannot find yourself, try the local spelling of your name and its different Latin spellings.

ClayArena takes the results from the competition's score sheets: the official sheets where the referee records each target as broken or missed. So the most important check happens at the ground, not on the site. Your profile will show exactly what the referee wrote down.

html.sporting: Check your score on the card (in Sporting™ this is the squad's score sheet) when you leave each stand. If it is wrong, tell the referee at once: only the referee decides, and that decision cannot be appealed.
html.compak: Sign the score sheet at the end of each round. If you refuse to sign, no later complaint can be accepted.

body.html: Still see a mistake on the site? First contact the competition organiser: the organiser is responsible for the official results, and the site only shows them. If the problem is on the site itself, for example a misspelled name, write to the ClayArena team through the contacts on the site.

key_points.html: Open the competition and find yourself in the results table.
From the table you can open your shooter profile.
Search for your name as it is written in the competition documents: in the local alphabet or in Latin letters.
Check your score at the ground: in Sporting™ when you leave each stand, in Compak® Sporting when you sign the score sheet.

quiz.q: Where do the results on ClayArena come from?
quiz.explain: Results come from the score sheets, so check your score while you are still at the ground.

quiz.q: How many targets does an international Sporting™ competition usually have?
quiz.explain: The FITASC rules set 200 targets in rounds of 25 for international events.

quiz.q: You cannot find your name. What can you try?
quiz.explain: Names are written as in the competition documents: in Latin letters or in the local alphabet. The same surname can also be written in Latin letters in more than one way.
